assigned.title: A configured catalog with nothing usable does not look empty
assigned.acceptance: The user-facing catalog path preserves the distinction the port now makes between no_records_usable and catalog_empty. apps/web/src/lib/catalog.ts maps an empty array to 'empty' and therefore COLLAPSES THE TWO, which is the one place PL-0305's four-state work stops short of the user. The two states have different causes and different remedies: catalog_empty means the source has nothing, while no_records_usable means records exist and every one of them was withheld -- almost always for want of an operator rights basis, which is an operator action rather than a user problem. Required: catalog.ts consumes describeCatalog through requireCatalogDescription rather than inferring state from an empty array; a source that does not implement describeCatalog still works and is not reported as a failure, because the method is optional on the port by design; the user-facing copy for the withheld case does NOT promise the content is coming, since nobody has committed to obtaining those rights; and the withheld reasons are not leaked verbatim to the user, because they name internal policy vocabulary. A regression must drive both states through the real loader and observe different answers.
assigned.notes: Created 2026-09-20 on gpt-architect's round-52 direction when it approved PL-0305: 'Make sure the existing handoff has explicit ownership for ... If any is currently only prose with no task, create a narrow task before it can be forgotten.' PL-0305 is NOT to be reopened for any of these. Follow-up 3 of 4. Point 6 of the round-52 verdict.

typecheck.evidence: npx turbo run typecheck --force, exit 0, 11 of 11; npx tsc --noEmit in apps/web exit 0. The type split is load-bearing: CatalogLoadOutcome makes cause REQUIRED so a loader branch that forgets it is a compile error and page.tsx's Record over CatalogEmptyCause is total, while the wider CatalogLoadResult keeps cause optional so handler.test.ts's hand-built literals -- outside this task's surface -- still compile. Both are built from the same shared members so they cannot drift.

unit.evidence: npx turbo run test --force, exit 0, 20 of 20, 0 cached, 2642 passed 1 skipped. catalog.test.ts 33 passed (24 before); the six related suites 130 passed. TWO REDS OF DIFFERENT KINDS, REPORTED AS SUCH. Red 1 is a genuine value red: 'AssertionError: expected undefined to be catalog_empty' on a cause asserted against the unchanged loader. Red 2, the both-states regression, COULD NOT BE A VALUE RED THROUGH THE EMPTY PATH and the implementer said so plainly -- before the change the CatalogSource seam accepted only CatalogHomeResponse | null, which by construction carries no cause, so there was no input that would make the pre-change loader's two empty answers differ; the collapse was total, which IS the defect. What it produced instead was 'expected { status: error } to not deeply equal { status: error } -- Compared values have no visual difference'. NO WITHHELD VOCABULARY REACHES A RENDERER: readHomeCatalogFrom discards answer.withheld entirely and a test asserts JSON.stringify(result) contains none of rights_basis_not_declared, availability_not_stated, Q42 or Q7. TWO GUARDS BEYOND THE ASK: a source answering records_available whose records all have rights null is reported no_records_usable rather than catalog_empty, because works exist so 'the source has nothing' would be false; and catalog_empty from an answer with complete false is downgraded to cause_not_stated, because a prefix cannot support 'there is nothing there'. The implementer also DELETED 'No titles are currently available in your region', which asserted a cause nothing on the home path establishes, and flagged that as a judgement call rather than slipping it in. A source implementing no describeCatalog still loads and is not an error -- asserted, not assumed. NOT COVERED AND SAID SO: no test renders page.tsx, because apps/web has no React testing library and vitest runs environment node with no .test.tsx anywhere; the copy guarantee is enforced one level in, at the loader, and the does-not-promise property is a judgement published for the reviewer.

assigned.reviewDependencyAdded: apps/web/src/lib/catalog-ingestion-source.ts added to reviewDependencies 2026-09-20, on the implementer's own report. requireCatalogDescription -- which this task's acceptance names by name as the thing catalog.ts must consume -- lives in that file, and the declaration did not list it, so the approval would have fingerprinted a reviewed surface that omitted the accessor the whole task turns on. A read, not a write: reviewDependencies widens what an approval covers without reserving the path.
